editorial_thesis: The most useful new signal is operational: physical AI is closing the evidence-to-intervention loop, mobile platforms are turning security into layered defaults, and agent developers are open-sourcing the contract layer around tools and SDKs.

topic_groups.title: Physical AI Operations
topic_groups.selection_rationale: A fresh deployment-oriented signal: robotics tooling is moving from lab visualization toward agentic data triage, remote intervention, and auditable learning loops.

sources.title: Agentic Data Platform for Physical AI
sources.why_selected: Unifies collection, search, comparison, curation, and agent-assisted reasoning over multimodal robot data.
sources.usefulness: Prototype an evidence-backed incident workspace: every answer cites topic, timestamp, or schema; every proposed dataset change is reviewable.

sources.title: Foxglove goes agentic
sources.why_selected: Adds an in-app agent sidebar plus MCP so external agents can search recordings, build layouts, write scripts, and diagnose data.
sources.usefulness: Use MCP as a reference for controlled cross-application actions with local tools, cloud tools, skills, and evals separated.

sources.title: Remote Visualization & Teleoperation
sources.why_selected: Streams live telemetry/video and supports intervention over lossy LTE, Wi-Fi, and VPN links.
sources.usefulness: Useful pattern for client field operations: degrade gracefully, preserve operator visibility, and keep control paths explicit.

sources.title: Remote Access generally available
sources.why_selected: Uses device tokens, short-lived credentials, and WebRTC/SFU relaying so robots behind firewalls can be viewed and controlled.
sources.usefulness: Borrow the connection model for secure remote workers: outbound-only gateway, short-lived session grants, independent viewer quality.

sources.title: Introducing Semantic Search
sources.why_selected: Searches image/video topics with natural-language scene descriptions and previews.
sources.usefulness: A model for searching Buildn’s artifact corpus by behavior and outcome rather than filename or tag alone.

topic_groups.title: Mobile Security + Privacy
topic_groups.selection_rationale: The current Android bulletin combines an urgent patch obligation with a broader shift toward on-device detection, granular permissions, and privacy-preserving forensics.

sources.title: Android Security Bulletin — September 2026
sources.why_selected: The 2026-09-05 level addresses a critical system vulnerability enabling remote code execution without privileges or user interaction.
sources.usefulness: Turn patch-level evidence into a recurring client readiness check and an explicit exception queue.

sources.title: Android Security and Privacy in 2026
sources.why_selected: Adds live threat detection, verified financial calls, USB protection, intrusion logging, granular permissions, and hardware-backed AI privacy controls.
sources.usefulness: Use as a reference architecture for defense-in-depth around agent devices and sensitive personal context.

sources.title: September Android Drop
sources.why_selected: Introduces remembered items in Find Hub, Guided vision, Motion Assist, and collaborative Keep inside Messages.
sources.usefulness: Shows how ambient memory and multimodal assistance can be useful when scoped to a clear user task and reversible record.

sources.title: September Pixel Drop
sources.why_selected: Adds Pixel-specific VIP, scam-detection, and Pixel Watch capabilities in the September release.
sources.usefulness: A practical reminder that security UX lands through device-level defaults and small, repeated interventions.

sources.title: Android 17 features
sources.why_selected: Combines temporary location/contact access, theft recovery, stronger PIN throttling, and expanded threat detection.
sources.usefulness: Translate temporary access and recovery modes into agent permissions that expire by task, not by vague role.

topic_groups.title: Open Agent Developer Infrastructure
topic_groups.selection_rationale: A neglected infrastructure lane earned inclusion because fresh Google and GitHub releases expose a practical boundary: use agents for customization, but keep formal interfaces deterministic and inspectable.

sources.title: Why client SDK generation belongs in the open
sources.why_selected: Google and Speakeasy open-sourced an AGPL OpenAPI generator for multi-language SDKs, agent-friendly CLIs, and documentation MCP servers.
sources.usefulness: A direct pattern for turning stable API contracts into tools agents can call without inventing temporary HTTP scripts.

sources.title: Agent Anomaly Detection
sources.why_selected: Asynchronously analyzes reasoning traces, tool calls, logs, and OpenTelemetry to surface suspicious but superficially successful sessions.
sources.usefulness: Use the layered detector pattern: statistical scan, deeper reasoning, then reconstructed evidence and policy action.

sources.title: The Anatomy of Harness Engineering
sources.why_selected: Google frames coding-agent reliability as a harness problem: evaluation, iteration, guardrails, and environment design around the model.
sources.usefulness: Supports treating worker harnesses as versioned, testable product assets—not prompt text hidden in infrastructure.

sources.title: ADK for Kotlin 1.0
sources.why_selected: Brings production-ready agent development primitives to Kotlin, Android, and adjacent JVM workflows.
sources.usefulness: Useful for client work where agent interaction must live close to mobile lifecycle, identity, and device permissions.

sources.title: Genkit Go 1.0
sources.why_selected: Makes Genkit Go a stable path for building and instrumenting AI features in Go services.
sources.usefulness: A credible option for small, observable worker services where low operational overhead matters.
